goals.title: Prelims GS: Polity I + II
goals.detail: October 2026 · Primary source: Vajiram Yellow Books Polity I + II (about 584 pages). Complete one static pass; make concise Constitution, institutions and governance notes; solve PYQs after major topics. Plan roughly 12–13 hours/week for static reading and 3–4 hours/week for PYQs/revision; keep current affairs integrated rather than creating a separate block.

goals.title: Paper I: Linear Algebra foundations
goals.detail: Start with the December 2022 IMS notes as the conceptual spine. Cover vector spaces and subspaces, basis/dimension, linear transformations, matrices and rank. Keep a proof/problem error log and measure progress by mastered topics, worked problems and PYQs rather than page count.

goals.title: Weeks 1–4: coding + Java baseline + first system design
goals.detail: 13.5 h/week. W1: timed coding baseline; arrays/hash maps; Java collections, equals/hashCode and immutability; HLD answer template. W2: strings, frequency maps and two pointers; requirements, estimates, APIs/data model; SQL SELECT/WHERE/GROUP BY. W3: sorting/sliding window; Spring Boot REST skeleton; typed agent-tool loop; AWS IAM/least privilege. W4: binary search; OS process/thread basics; SQL joins; VPC/subnets/security groups. Outputs: baseline/error log, URL-shortener design, tested health-endpoint API and capstone scope/safety non-goals. Gate: solve two unseen array/hash-map problems in 60 minutes and design the URL shortener without notes.

goals.title: DayFlow: Offline PDF plans library — bundle and verify
goals.detail: October 2026 · Keep the five source plan PDFs available from More → Plans & Documents with the built-in offline reader: Unified Master Execution Plan, UPSC GS Monthly Plan, Job Switch Master Plan, the previous EM interview plan and Technical Interview Readiness — Spoon-Fed Plan. The Roadmap is driven by plans_catalog.json, not by parsing PDF bytes. Do not mark this goal complete until all five originals are packaged, each entry opens the correct file, and all render in airplane mode on a physical device.
previousDetails: October 2026 · Make the four saved plan PDFs accessible inside DayFlow from More → Plans & Documents, without an internet connection. Current implementation: the library screen and navigation exist, but the screen shows concise reading copies rather than the original PDFs. Remaining work: bundle the original Unified Master Execution Plan, UPSC 2027 Prelims GS Monthly Plan, 2027 EM 6/9-Month Master Plan and 2027 EM Interview Readiness Plan as local app assets; update each entry to open its original PDF; build the APK and verify all four open in airplane mode. Keep this goal open until original-file access and offline verification pass.

goals.title: Prelims GS: Modern, Ancient and Medieval History
goals.detail: November 2026 · Primary sources: Vajiram Modern History (about 296 pages), Ancient History (about 140) and Medieval History (about 103), approximately 539 pages combined. Build chronology/theme notes and use PYQs to identify examinable causes, outcomes, movements and contributors; avoid elaborate note-making.

goals.title: Paper I: Calculus and remaining Linear Algebra
goals.detail: Continue linear transformations, eigenvalues/eigenvectors and matrix methods; build limits, continuity, differentiability, mean-value results and single-variable integration. Attempt selected problems without looking at worked solutions; retain difficult proofs for spaced revision.

goals.title: Weeks 5–8: concurrency + trees + backend persistence
goals.detail: W5 linked lists, JVM/GC concepts and PostgreSQL CRUD. W6 stacks/queues, executors/synchronization, tests for invalid input/concurrency. W7 recursion/tree traversals, composition, caching/consistency. W8 trees/BST, SOLID, retries/timeouts/idempotency, SQL joins/subqueries, RDS and retrieval grounding. Outputs: tested CRUD API, migrations, one rate-limiter HLD. Gate: solve 3/4 representative tree problems and run integration tests from a clean DB.

goals.title: Prelims GS: Environment + Art & Culture
goals.detail: December 2026 · Primary sources: Vajiram Environment & Ecology (about 307 pages) and NEXT IAS Art & Culture (about 184), approximately 491 pages combined. Keep factual material in compact revision sheets; connect ecology, biodiversity and conservation concepts to PYQs and current events.

goals.title: Paper I: Analytic Geometry + Ordinary Differential Equations
goals.detail: Cover lines, planes and standard curves/surfaces, followed by first- and higher-order ordinary differential equations and standard solution methods. Maintain a worked-problem/error log and revisit prerequisites whenever solutions fail.

goals.title: Weeks 9–13: heaps, graphs, SQL depth + first technical mock
goals.detail: W9 heaps/top-K/greedy, CTEs/windows, CloudWatch and request IDs. W10 BFS/DFS/components, sharding/hot keys, citations/abstention. W11 topological sort/shortest path, OS scheduling/deadlocks, rate limiting. W12 selected 1-D DP, virtual memory, EXPLAIN/indexes. W13 mixed review and 45-min coding + 45-min HLD mock; recap IAM/VPC/EC2/S3/RDS and agent validation/stopping rules. Outputs: SQL drill, observable request path and top-five technical weakness list. Gate: complete mock without notes and choose next work from actual misses.

goals.title: Prelims GS: Physical/World + Indian Geography
goals.detail: January 2027 · Primary source: NEXT IAS Physical & World Geography (about 211 pages) plus Indian Geography & Disaster Management (about 382), approximately 593 pages. Prioritise concepts, maps and diagrams. This is the heaviest month by page count; keep notes short and use topic-wise PYQs.

goals.title: Paper I: Dynamics and Statics
goals.detail: Cover motion, work and energy, equilibrium, forces, potential energy and standard dynamics/statics problem types. Practise derivations and timed numerical questions; integrate these with previously studied Calculus rather than treating them as isolated formulas.

goals.title: Weeks 14–17: LLD + HLD + distributed systems depth
goals.detail: W14 class responsibilities, interfaces, composition, SOLID and testability. W15 messaging/chat HLD: delivery semantics, queues, retries, deduplication and idempotency. W16 feed/recommendation HLD: freshness, ranking, caching and evaluation; create 20 fixed agent-evaluation cases. W17 TCP/DNS/HTTP/TLS, timeouts, consensus/Paxos at interview depth; distinguish replication, partitioning and consensus. Outputs: two blank-page designs, one tested LLD implementation and concise trade-off notes. Use InterviewReady Advanced only for material not already mastered in Simplified.

goals.title: Prelims GS: Indian Economy
goals.detail: February 2027 · Primary source: NEXT IAS Indian Economy (about 467 pages). Study mechanisms rather than terminology alone: concept → mechanism → Indian application → PYQ. Consolidate budgeting, growth, inclusion, agriculture and related economic institutions with mixed practice.

goals.title: Paper I: Vector Analysis + integration of Paper I
goals.detail: Cover grad, div, curl, line/surface/volume integrals and the major integral theorems. Consolidate Linear Algebra, Calculus, Analytic Geometry, ODE, Dynamics/Statics and Vector Analysis; identify syllabus gaps before moving into Paper II.

goals.title: Weeks 18–21: AWS reliability + AI security + capstone
goals.detail: W18 deployment/reliability, IAM, network boundaries, RDS resilience, CloudWatch, backups and cost. W19 agent state/workflows, prompt injection, tool poisoning, least privilege, approval gates and sandboxing. W20 integrate one vertical slice: task → approved-file retrieval → structured proposal, with unsafe actions blocked. W21 benchmark 30–50 fixed cases, inspect traces, measure failures/latency/cost where feasible, and run a second coding/design mock. Outputs: reproducible tests, threat model, evaluation record and runbook draft.

goals.title: Prelims GS: General Science + Science & Technology
goals.detail: March 2027 · Primary sources: NEXT IAS General Science (about 135 pages) and Science & Technology (about 231), approximately 366 pages. Finish the static source set by 31 March; use remaining time for cumulative PYQs, revision and backlog clearance. The page counts are edition-dependent planning figures.

goals.title: Paper I closure + Paper II Algebra foundations
goals.detail: Audit every Paper I unit against the UPSC syllabus, attempt representative PYQs and close high-impact gaps. Begin Paper II Algebra: groups/rings and core algebraic structures, notation and standard proofs. Update the error log from timed work.

goals.title: Weeks 22–26: consolidate core skills + six-month readiness gate
goals.detail: Planned effort to this gate: 351 hours. W22 consolidate arrays/strings/sliding-window/binary-search. W23 trees/graphs plus an HLD with failure modes. W24 timed SQL and targeted OS/networking/DBMS. W25 full technical rehearsal: coding, HLD, LLD, backend deep-dive, AWS/operations and AI security. W26 final scorecard and capstone walkthrough. Gate: timed coding; independent HLD/LLD; Java/Spring explanation; SQL/core-CS recall; AWS deploy/security/monitor/rollback explanation; bounded agent with retrieval grounding, fixed evaluation and security controls. Apply when demonstrated gates are met; otherwise fix the highest-impact gap instead of restarting every course.

goals.title: Prelims conversion: static revision + PYQs
goals.detail: April 2027 · No new static-source pages planned. Cycle through Polity, History, Environment/Art & Culture, Geography, Economy and Science/S&T using active recall, PYQs and the error log. Revise current-affairs links and prioritise the weakest subjects.

goals.title: Prelims test conversion: GS mocks, CSAT and MCQs
goals.detail: April target from the saved plan: 6–8 GS mocks, 4–6 CSAT tests and approximately 700–900 GS MCQs/PYQs. Review every wrong answer and distinguish knowledge gaps, misreading, elimination errors and time-pressure errors; adjust targets to actual performance.

goals.title: Paper II: Algebra + Real Analysis
goals.detail: Develop the first-pass checklist for groups/rings and real analysis, including sequences, series, convergence, continuity and standard proof techniques. Continue problem practice and retain a realistic recurring Maths block alongside Prelims-specific GS.

goals.title: Weeks 27–30: targeted gap repair
goals.detail: Use mock/error-log evidence, not the whole syllabus. W27 targeted TUF coding patterns; re-solve misses after 48 hours. W28 redo two HLDs from blank pages with estimates, APIs/data models, bottlenecks, failure modes, observability and trade-offs. W29 Java/Spring deep dive: transactions, persistence, concurrency, security, testing, performance and root-cause analysis. W30 AWS scenarios: database outage, bad deployment, high latency, recovery, rollback and cost/security. Outputs: coding post-mortem, two recorded designs, seeded-bug investigation and operations tabletop.

goals.title: Prelims final revision: rapid recall + weak areas
goals.detail: May 1–22, 2027 · No new static reading. Use short revision loops, PYQs, current-affairs consolidation and the error log. Prioritise recall speed, accuracy and recovery from repeated mistakes over making new notes.

goals.title: Final Prelims simulations · exam target 23 May 2027
goals.detail: Saved-plan target for 1–22 May: 4–5 GS mocks and 2–3 CSAT mocks, with final rapid revision and exam simulations. Complete and review each mock; protect sleep and logistics in the final days. The source plan lists UPSC CSE Prelims for 23 May 2027.

goals.title: Paper II: Complex Analysis + Linear Programming
goals.detail: Cover analytic functions, Cauchy results, singularities/residues and standard contour-integration questions; build the LP checklist for simplex, duality and related methods. These topics are in the longer CSE optional plan, not in the Prelims GS PDF.

goals.title: Weeks 31–34: agent evaluation/security + harder coding/HLD
goals.detail: W31 improve fixed evaluation cases, traces, regression tests, failure taxonomy and cost/latency observations. W32 test prompt injection, tool poisoning, path traversal, secret leakage, excessive permissions and unbounded loops. W33 harder company-relevant coding and a timed mock. W34 study two unique InterviewReady Advanced case studies matched to target JDs; explain them from first principles, including bottlenecks and failures. Outputs: benchmark comparison, security report, coding score and two case-study walkthroughs.

goals.title: Mains GS-I: history, culture, society and geography
goals.detail: June 2027 · Resume the wider Mains-oriented syllabus after the Prelims phase. Map Indian culture, modern/post-independence history, world history, society and geography against the official syllabus. Build concise topic sheets and begin structured answer practice; distinguish this phase from the completed Prelims static pass.

goals.title: Paper II: Partial Differential Equations
goals.detail: Cover standard PDE methods, canonical forms and representative problem types. Build a topic checklist, solve selected previous-year questions, and revisit Calculus/ODE prerequisites where errors recur.

goals.title: Weeks 35–39: LLD + company alignment + full technical mocks
goals.detail: Planned effort to this gate: 526.5 hours. W35 timed LLD/machine-coding exercise with tests and extension points. W36 map 3–5 target JDs to coding, backend, HLD/LLD, databases, AWS/operations and AI requirements. W37 technical mock loop A across coding, HLD, LLD, backend, cloud and AI/agentic depth. W38 repeat with unseen questions/different design and repair critical failures. W39 final scorecard, architecture diagram, test/evaluation evidence, project walkthrough and runbook. Decide applications or remediation from observed performance, not course completion.

goals.title: Mains GS-II: Constitution, governance, social justice + IR
goals.detail: July 2027 · Work through Constitution/polity, governance, accountability, welfare and social-justice themes, India’s neighbourhood and international relations. Practise concise, structured Mains answers and connect institutions, current affairs and case examples.

goals.title: Paper II: Numerical Analysis
goals.detail: Cover interpolation, numerical integration, numerical solutions of equations and ODE methods from the selected syllabus/source. Practise representative questions and track method selection, numerical accuracy and time.

goals.title: Technical interview execution: applications + feedback-led repairs
goals.detail: Track target roles and interview outcomes. After each interview, classify gaps across coding, HLD/LLD, backend, databases, cloud/operations or AI. Pick weekly practice from recurring evidence. Keep Java/JVM, DSA, design and production reasoning warm; add a course only for a named gap.

goals.title: Mains GS-III: economy, agriculture, S&T, environment + security
goals.detail: August 2027 · Cover economic development, agriculture, science and technology, environment/biodiversity, disaster management and internal security. Use issue-based notes and practise answers that link concepts, evidence, government action and trade-offs.

goals.title: Paper II: Computer Programming
goals.detail: Cover number systems, Boolean logic, algorithms/flowcharts and the listed programming fundamentals. Practise explaining algorithm steps and solving syllabus-aligned questions; treat this as one part of Paper II, not a substitute for mathematical problem practice.

goals.title: Target-company technical loops
goals.detail: Match technical preparation to active job descriptions. Rotate timed coding, independent HLD/LLD, Java/Spring and database deep-dives, cloud/production scenarios and capstone/agent walkthrough. Record score, time, hints and failed follow-ups; pick the three highest-value gaps for the next week.

goals.title: Mains GS-IV: ethics, probity + Essay practice
goals.detail: September 2027 · Cover ethics, values, attitude, emotional intelligence, probity, public-service dilemmas and case studies. Practise essay outlines and full answers under time limits; keep separate examples and concepts easy to recall.

goals.title: Paper I: timed sectional tests + PYQ repair
goals.detail: Attempt timed Paper I sections covering Linear Algebra, Calculus, Analytic Geometry, ODE, Dynamics/Statics and Vector Analysis. Review solution structure, accuracy and time; re-solve missed questions without the original solution.

goals.title: Technical readiness review from real outcomes
goals.detail: Review actual interview results, technical feedback and role fit. Track coding accuracy/time, design quality, backend reasoning, SQL/core-CS recall, operations scenarios and capstone questions. Decide whether to continue applications, repair a specific skill or narrow target roles; set a finite next checkpoint.

goals.title: Mains GS-I/II consolidation + answer writing
goals.detail: October 2027 · Revisit History, Culture, Geography, Society, Constitution, Governance, Social Justice and IR. Use PYQs to select high-frequency themes, practise timed answers and repair weak content/structure.

goals.title: Paper II: Mechanics + Fluid Dynamics
goals.detail: Cover Lagrangian/Hamiltonian mechanics, continuity and standard fluid-flow concepts from the selected syllabus. Record essential assumptions and derivation steps; practise representative problems and identify remaining coverage gaps.

goals.title: Role-specific coding + system-design refresh
goals.detail: Use active job descriptions and interview feedback to choose a limited set of coding patterns and system designs. Reproduce solutions from scratch, practise follow-up changes and refresh Java/Spring, databases, reliability and cost trade-offs only where role-relevant.

goals.title: Mains GS-III/IV consolidation + Essay
goals.detail: November 2027 · Revise economy, agriculture, S&T, environment, security, ethics and probity. Practise timed GS-III/IV answers, ethics case studies and essay outlines; keep an error log of factual, analytical and structural weaknesses.

goals.title: Paper II sectional tests + PYQ gap closure
goals.detail: Attempt timed sections across Algebra, Real/Complex Analysis, Linear Programming, PDE, Numerical Analysis, Computer Programming, Mechanics and Fluid Dynamics. Re-solve incorrect questions and target the three largest recurring weaknesses.

goals.title: Focused gap closure from technical interview evidence
goals.detail: Repair the most frequent, highest-impact technical failures. Prefer deliberate practice and retests over broad new courses. Check improvement across multiple unseen problems/designs and technical follow-ups.

goals.title: Full CSE syllabus audit + mixed tests
goals.detail: December 2027 · Audit tracked GS topics and the broader Mains syllabus, complete mixed PYQ/test sets and revise the weakest areas. Schedule any remaining first-pass work explicitly for the January checkpoint rather than treating unchecked topics as complete.

goals.title: Mixed Paper I/II PYQs + first-pass closure
goals.detail: Attempt mixed timed questions from both papers, consolidate formula/result sheets and close high-priority syllabus gaps. Compare topic mastery, solved PYQs and the error log; do not equate reading a topic with exam readiness.

goals.title: Technical pipeline review + targeted preparation
goals.detail: Review roles, interview feedback and remaining technical-fit gaps. Refresh only topics needed by active opportunities; maintain coding/design fluency and keep project claims factual. Do not add technologies without a target-role reason.

goals.title: 1 January checkpoint: verify CSE syllabus coverage
goals.detail: By 1 January 2028, audit every tracked GS and Mains syllabus item against actual coverage. Name unresolved topics explicitly, review test/PYQ evidence and set the next revision schedule. This checkpoint measures coverage; it does not automatically mark topics complete.

goals.title: 1 January checkpoint: verify Paper I + II first pass
goals.detail: Audit both Maths Optional papers against the syllabus and the IMS-note plan. List topics mastered, topics needing revision, PYQs attempted and unresolved problem types; schedule remaining work explicitly. Use performance evidence, not page counts alone.

goals.title: Career roadmap reset from technical outcomes
goals.detail: Use applications, scores, feedback and role requirements to define the next technical cycle. Record strengths and gaps across coding, HLD/LLD, Java/backend, databases, cloud/operations and AI/agentic work. Set a finite checkpoint; checklist completion is not an offer guarantee.

documents.title: Unified Master Execution Plan
documents.subtitle: October 2026 – January 2028 · Combined execution system
documents.content:
MASTER EXECUTION PLAN | OCT 2026 – JAN 2028

PURPOSE
Coordinate UPSC CSE preparation, software-career progression, health, and DayFlow in one execution system. Review progress regularly and adjust based on evidence rather than adding complexity.

UPSC CSE
Keep General Studies and Maths Optional as distinct study tracks. Use monthly subject targets, practice questions, revision, and progress tracking. The dedicated GS monthly plan is the source for month-by-month subject assignments.

SOFTWARE CAREER
Prepare for an engineering-management transition using a staged 6–9 month plan. Build interview readiness through system design, technical depth, leadership examples, and structured practice. Use the dedicated interview-readiness plan for the focused preparation track.

HEALTH AND REVIEW
Review weekly averages and adherence. Every four weeks review weight trend, waist, training tolerance, sleep, and relevant medical guidance. Reassess body-composition estimates every 8–12 weeks if useful, using a consistent method and allowing for measurement error. If adherence is poor, simplify the plan before making it stricter.

DAYFLOW RULES
Identify weekday versus weekend and allow WFH/WFO switching. “Modify & Save Today’s Routine” edits only the selected date, never a reusable template. Distinguish fixed and flexible blocks. Track planned versus actual time and commute with minimal taps. Progress percentages must use the same source of truth as the detailed progress view. During March–May 2027, prioritize correctness blockers over cosmetic redesigns or new features.

REVIEW CADENCE
Weekly: review 7-day weight average, exercise, adherence, hunger/energy, and study load. Every four weeks: review weight trend, waist, training tolerance, sleep, and medical guidance. Every 8–12 weeks: review body-composition estimates if useful.

This is a concise offline reading copy. The original master PDF contains the complete tables, monthly detail, and references.

UPSC 2027 PRELIMS | GENERAL STUDIES MONTHLY PLAN

OCTOBER 2026 — POLITY
Primary source: Vajiram Polity I + II. Listed source volume: 584 pages. Complete the main polity source once and use previous-year questions immediately after major constitutional topics.

NOVEMBER 2026 — HISTORY
Primary source: Vajiram Modern (296 pages), Ancient (140 pages), and Medieval (103 pages); 539 pages total. Avoid over-noting. Build chronology and themes, then use PYQs to distinguish examinable material from low-return detail.

DECEMBER 2026 — ENVIRONMENT + ART & CULTURE
Primary source: Vajiram Environment (307 pages) and NEXT Art & Culture (184 pages); 491 pages total. Compress factual material into short revision sheets.

EXECUTION PRINCIPLES
Use the source plan’s monthly assignments as the schedule of record. Pair reading with PYQs, keep notes concise, and reserve time for revision and factual consolidation. Do not silently substitute a different source or monthly subject sequence.

This offline copy preserves the opening monthly entries available in the source extract. The original PDF contains the remaining monthly assignments and detailed execution notes.

documents.title: 2027 Job Switch — EM 6–9 Month Master Plan
documents.subtitle: Career transition roadmap and staged preparation
documents.content:
2027 JOB SWITCH | ENGINEERING MANAGEMENT | 6–9 MONTH MASTER PLAN

OBJECTIVE
Prepare for a software engineering management opportunity through a staged plan while keeping UPSC preparation and daily execution sustainable. The master plan coordinates career preparation with the wider October 2026–January 2028 execution timeline.

STAGED TARGET
Around month 6: begin interviewing for Tier 3 and Tier 4 target companies to measure readiness and identify gaps. Around month 9: aim to be a stronger candidate for Tier 1 and Tier 2 targets.

PREPARATION TRACKS
Build evidence for technical depth, system design, architecture decisions, difficult debugging, production ownership, project execution, people leadership, and behavioral interviews. Use practice interviews and review weak areas rather than relying on preparation hours alone.

ALIGNMENT
Keep the company shortlist aligned with compensation goals and preparation constraints. Evaluate roles against actual scope and experience; do not assume an Engineering Manager title or compensation level is guaranteed.

This is a concise offline reading copy. The original master PDF contains the full roadmap, company tiers, and detailed scheduling.

documents.title: 2027 Job Switch — EM Interview Readiness Plan
documents.subtitle: Focused technical, system-design, leadership and interview preparation
documents.content:
2027 JOB SWITCH | ENGINEERING MANAGEMENT INTERVIEW READINESS

PURPOSE
A focused plan for preparing for engineering-management interviews over a 6–9 month window. Use it alongside the job-switch master plan; it is the interview-preparation track, not a replacement for the wider roadmap.

CORE PREPARATION
• System design and architecture trade-offs.
• Technical depth and difficult debugging.
• Production ownership, reliability, and incident reasoning.
• Project execution, prioritization, and cross-functional collaboration.
• Leadership, conflict resolution, feedback, and behavioral examples.
• Mock interviews, review of gaps, and repeated practice.

READINESS CHECKPOINTS
Use Tier 3/4 interviews as a diagnostic checkpoint around month 6. Use the evidence to close gaps before targeting Tier 1/2 roles around month 9. Assess readiness from interview performance and feedback, not calendar time alone.

This is a concise offline reading copy. Consult the original interview-readiness PDF for the complete schedule, exercises, and detailed checkpoints.

documents.title: Technical Interview Readiness — Spoon-Fed Plan
documents.subtitle: 39 weeks · 13.5 hours/week · 351-hour six-month gate · 526.5-hour nine-month gate
documents.content:
TECHNICAL INTERVIEW READINESS — SPOON-FED EXECUTION PLAN

PURPOSE
Technical interview workstream only. Course completion is not the goal: choose modules based on interview value and measured gaps.

TIME BUDGET
13.5 hours/week: three WFH blocks × 1.5h, two WFO blocks × 1.5h, two weekend blocks × 3h. This is 351 hours over 26 weeks and 526.5 hours over 39 weeks. Preserve protected UPSC study time.

FIXED WEEKLY BLOCKS
• WFH 1: TUF coding 60 min + Java/backend 30 min.
• WFH 2: AI/agentic roadmap 60 min + capstone/evaluation/security 30 min.
• WFH 3: backend/capstone 60 min + coding error-log review 30 min.
• WFO 1: OS/networking/DBMS/SQL 45 min + timed recall/questions 45 min.
• WFO 2: InterviewReady system design 75 min + notes from memory 15 min.
• Weekend 1: AWS 75 min + backend/capstone 75 min + tests/docs 30 min.
• Weekend 2: TUF coding 75 min + HLD/LLD 60 min + AI evaluation/security or technical mock 45 min.
Every block must produce solved problems, tests, a design, an evaluation result, an operations note or a logged weakness—not passive watching alone.

MONTH 1 / WEEKS 1–4
Arrays/hash maps, strings/two pointers, sorting/sliding window, binary search; Java collections/OOP/immutability; HLD framework; SQL basics; OS process/thread basics; Spring Boot health endpoint; agent loop and IAM. Outputs: baseline, URL-shortener design, tested API and capstone safety scope.

MONTH 2 / WEEKS 5–8
Linked lists, stacks/queues, concurrency, recursion/trees/BST; JVM/GC; PostgreSQL CRUD, validation, migrations, integration tests; joins/subqueries, cache/consistency, retries/idempotency; RDS and retrieval grounding. Output: running tested API and rate-limiter HLD.

MONTH 3 / WEEKS 9–13
Heaps/greedy, graph BFS/DFS/topological sort, selected 1-D DP; SQL CTEs/windows/EXPLAIN/indexes; OS virtual memory; observability, sharding and grounded retrieval; first coding + HLD simulation. Output: observable API, SQL drill and top-five weakness list.

MONTH 4 / WEEKS 14–17
LLD/SOLID, messaging/chat HLD, feed/recommendation HLD, TCP/DNS/HTTP/TLS and interview-level consensus. Use Advanced for gaps only; add a fixed agent evaluation set. Output: two blank-page designs and a tested LLD implementation.

MONTH 5 / WEEKS 18–21
AWS reliability/deployment; agent state, prompt injection/tool poisoning/least privilege/sandboxing; integrated capstone vertical slice; 30–50 fixed evaluation cases; second technical mock. Output: reproducible tests, threat model, evaluation record and runbook draft.

MONTH 6 / WEEKS 22–26
Consolidate coding; trees/graphs; timed SQL and targeted OS/networking/DBMS; full technical rehearsal; final readiness gate. Require timed coding, independent HLD/LLD, Java/backend explanation, SQL/core-CS recall, AWS operations explanation and a bounded tested/evaluated agent. Apply when gates are met or target the highest-impact gaps.

MONTH 7 / WEEKS 27–30
Targeted coding repair; redo HLD from blank pages; backend deep dive in transactions, persistence, concurrency, security, testing and performance; AWS incident/rollback/recovery scenarios.

MONTH 8 / WEEKS 31–34
Agent evaluation and security regression; adversarial tests; harder company-relevant coding; two unique Advanced case studies matched to target JDs.

MONTH 9 / WEEKS 35–39
Timed LLD/machine coding; map 3–5 target JDs to technical evidence; two technical mock loops across coding, HLD, LLD, backend, cloud/operations and AI; final scorecard, architecture diagram, tests, evaluation evidence and runbook.

RESOURCE RULES
TUF Pinnacle: selected DSA order—arrays/hash maps/strings, two pointers/sliding window, binary search, linked lists/stacks/queues, trees/BST, heaps/greedy, graphs, selected DP. Do not chase all 474 A2Z problems. Prioritize OS processes/threads/synchronization/deadlocks/memory; TCP/DNS/HTTP/TLS/timeouts; DB indexes/transactions/isolation/recovery/query optimization.
InterviewReady Simplified: primary first pass for requirements/estimates, APIs/data model, database/cache/networking, replication/consistency, queues, rate limiting, security, observability and trade-offs. Reproduce selected designs from a blank page.
InterviewReady Advanced: gap-driven only; unique distributed-system/NoSQL/migration/tracing concepts and relevant case studies.
AI/agentic: typed tools and bounded loops → validation/stopping rules → retrieval/grounding → state/idempotency → fixed eval/traces → prompt injection/tool poisoning/least privilege/sandboxing/approval. Defer fine-tuning or GPU serving unless target JDs require it.
AWS: IAM, VPC/subnets/security groups, EC2, S3, RDS, CloudWatch, resilience, backups, access control, cost and deployment/rollback. Keep Kubernetes/Terraform introductory unless target JDs demand depth.
Capstone: scoped Repository Reliability Platform + bounded engineering task agent, approved-file retrieval, structured proposal, isolated test execution, diff/evidence review, human approval before side effects, Docker/logs/traces and AWS where practical.
